items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Emil Bigard, his uncle, was a violin player.

ctx.x: onwards and all them bands had uniforms. They had about, they had eight, nine-piece bands like that. That's the way they used to run. Big bands, heavy bands. Every one of them had, would have different colored uniforms. And one band had a brown, brown, brown uniform. Now Chicken, he played with one of them bands. I'm trying to think now. You know Chicken the trombone player? Chicken Henry, yeah. Well Chicken can give you more ideas about me and me now because he, he can maybe remember them bands because he played…

you know, for a long time ago. Yeah. Well, well, uh, you knew the, Emil, huh? Emil Bigard, his uncle, was a violin player. Well, I don't remember him. Didn't he? I think, I think he played around. So, Alex would know even from the time he was a little boy. Who was the first saxophone player you heard? Who? The very first saxophone player. Oh, well, I wouldn't know it.

No. That's been way long before my time. I wouldn't. They had saxes a long time ago. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I wouldn't know who the first one, but I know they had so many of them, you know. What was that, what was that Blaze Away band? That was a band that, uh, come from over the river. I don't remember that at all. They had an organized band like that. They had cards printed and everything, but it was pretty good, but they didn't last long. They went to pieces. Did you know the guys? No. Oh, it must have been so…
